source_title: The 30 best conspiracy thrillers of all time, ranked - Entertainment Weekly
source_excerpt:
Bettmann Archive; Myles Aronowitz/Warner Bros.; Universal Studios
In the ’80s, there was a push to censor certain horror films or at least shame the people who made them. In Britain, you had the notorious list of so-called video nasties, and in the U.S., you had revered critics like Gene Siskel and Roger Ebert condemning slashers, suggesting the films were unethical and bad for developing minds.
Decades later, horror films are recognized as an important artistic outlet for confronting fears and trauma, and many would agree that top-down censorship of anything is only going to make it more popular. However! There’s another type of movie that taps into an arguably more unsettling fear — the possibility that a grand conspiracy is unfolding, and only one person knows the truth. In real life, that kind of conviction can be dangerous. On screen, it can be thrilling.
There’s nothing quite like a good paranoid conspiracy thriller . It’s one of the best microgenres in cinema, and we are happy to recommend 30 great ones for you to add to your watchlist.
The aliens aren’t coming, they are already here. This special effects-heavy summer spectacle paired Will Smith and Tommy Lee Jones as two sharply dressed government agents tasked with keeping facts about extraterrestrial life under wraps with snappy dialogue and big action set pieces . Best is the final reveal that our entire known universe is just a marble in some higher being’s sack of toys.
Where to watch Men in Black : Paramount+
One of the later works by John le Carré, this German-set slow-burn thriller is a master class in quiet deception for Philip Seymour Hoffman, who delivers one of his most intricate performances. The movie, with its crosses and double-crosses among agents in the War on Terror, is complex and even a little baffling until everything crashes together in its shocking final scene.
Where to watch A Most Wanted Man : Tubi
Greek filmmaker Costa-Gavras pushed the envelope for what a political thriller could achieve with this ripped-from-the-headlines finger-pointing thriller back in 1969. Deploying an international cast and slick production design, Z highlighted the crimes of an actual military coup, and drew audiences in with mystery elements and stylish editing.
Niko Tavernise/Universal Pictures and Amblin Entertainment
Steven Spielberg ’s most recent film balances his trademark wonderment with a strong dose of cynicism, suggesting that governments will gladly keep historically important discoveries a secret unless those with faith in humanity have the courage to act. So it is therefore up to you to race across the country, take over a television news station, and present space aliens to the wider public!
Where to watch Disclosure Day : Peacock
One of the lesser-known thrillers by Alfred Hitchcock , this one is set in the Netherlands (hence a set piece in a windmill) and features Joel McCrea as an American reporter in Europe discovering a massive spy ring filled with scoundrels and double agents. It features some of Hitchcock’s craftiest camerawork, and functions well as a sharp precursor to America’s involvement in World War II .
Where to watch Foreign Correspondent : HBO Max
Willem Dafoe plays a New Mexico sheriff who discovers a body and a briefcase full of cash in the desert, then impersonates the deceased to infiltrate a group of arms dealers. He soon enters a triangle (or maybe even a more complex shape) of deception among rival government agents. Costars include Samuel L. Jackson, Mary Elizabeth Mastrantonio, and Mickey Rourke.
Where to watch White Sands : Prime Video
Two wacky nuts think just because a powerful tech executive is a woman she must be from outer space! Oh, crap, they might be right. Bonkers Greek film director Yorgos Lanthimos is in peak form here, reteaming with Emma Stone as the possible interplanetary emissary, with Jesse Plemons and Aidan Delbis as the conspiracy theorists who get in over their heads when they take her hostage.
Mel Gibson plays a paranoid New York City cab driver who won’t stop blabbing about his conspiracy theories, one of which happens to be true. Suddenly Patrick Stewart (!) is after him and only Julia Roberts can help, for some reason. Gibson plays to his strengths as a weirdo who can’t stop talking in this entertaining late ’90s film.
Where to watch Conspiracy Theory : Tubi
The World Wide Web! A new place to share Grateful Dead setlists, compare Star Trek episodes and, of course, uncover grand conspiracies. Sandra Bullock is a lonely nerd who stumbles into a terrorist group and soon has her identity yanked from her. This paranoid thriller was perfectly timed to hit theaters just as the first America Online floppy disks appeared in mailboxes.
Where to watch The Net : Prime Video (to rent)
Italian director Francesco Rosi investigates the suspicious death of Enrico Mattei, the head of Italy’s state-owned oil company, who died in a mysterious plane crash in 1962. Gian Maria Volonté is mesmerizing as Mattei, a powerful industrialist who made enemies among international oil corporations. The film, which won the top prize at Cannes, blends actual documentary footage with reconstructed scenes to weave a complex narrative.
Where to watch The Mattei Affair : Prime Video (to rent)
O.J. Simpson in spaaaaaace! Ever since Apollo 11 landed on the moon, there have been people saying it didn’t happen. Capricorn One looks into what the U.S. government’s fallback would be if a manned mission to Mars went south, but they still needed the propaganda win. James Brolin, Sam Waterston, and Elliott Gould costar, as does Jerry Goldsmith’s spectacular original score.
Where to watch Capricorn One : Prime Video
FilmPublicityArchive/United Archives via Getty
The legendary hard-boiled film director Samuel Fuller follows Richard Widmark’s small-time pickpocket from New York City streets to the halls of power when he inadvertently palms secret microfilm meant for Communist spies. Thelma Ritter and gritty urban locations costar in this classic Cold War thriller.
Where to watch Pickup on South Street : Tubi
Toshiro Mifune marries the disabled daughter of his company’s corrupt exec in a long game to expose who is responsible for his father’s death. It’s a complex plan that quickly gets turned around when he catches feelings for the woman. Director Akira Kurosawa borrows elements from Shakespeare (as he frequently did), replacing Hamlet ’s medieval Denmark with Japanese post-war corporations.
Where to watch The Bad Sleep Well : Criterion Channel
When the U.S. president is accused of putting the moves on an underaged girl in the Oval Office right before an election, a spin doctor played by Robert De Niro is deployed to change the narrative. He hires a Hollywood producer played by Dustin Hoffman, and they drum up fake patriotism with a phony war. That the movie came out just weeks before the Clinton-Lewinsky scandal broke, with U.S. airstrikes in Sudan and Afghanistan following months later, could not have been more perfect.
Where to watch Wag the Dog : Prime Video (to rent)
Robert Aldrich’s quintessential film noir follows detective Mike Hammer (Ralph Meeker) as he gets entangled with a terrified woman and a glowing valise. What’s inside doesn’t really matter — it’s the Cold War in a box, with all the international machinations and horrifying double-crosses and conspiracies they represent.
Where to watch Kiss Me Deadly : Sling TV
The great Stanley Kubrick’s final film is a twisted adaptation of Arthur Schnitzler’s surreal novella concerning a shadow society of elites hosting depraved orgies in elegant settings. Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman star, and the production is notorious for being one of the longest continuous shoots in film history. Stories of Jeffrey Epstein, his jets filled with powerful names, and private islands of sexual captivity have kept this film extremely relevant.
Where to watch Eyes Wide Shut : HBO Max
It’s no conspiracy theory to say the CIA has had its hand in the machinations of Latin American governments. But it’s doubtful real life has ever been this funny. Peter Falk plays a loose-cannon spook who concocts an enormous scheme that involves robbing the U.S. mint, and drags along his meek soon-to-be-in-law, a New Jersey dentist played by Alan Arkin. Soon the two are racing around south of the equator, dodging bullets while zinging each other with jokes.
Will Smith plays a D.C. labor attorney who comes across evidence of a congressman’s assassination. He turns to a reluctant former intelligence operative played by Gene Hackman , then both of them must elude the full power of the surveillance state and its principal villain, Jon Voight. This taut Tony Scott thriller is a great look at early networked computer culture, much of which proved prophetic.
Where to watch Enemy of the State : Prime Video
Ever feel like someone is watching you? Peter Weir’s marvelous high-concept comedy-drama plops Jim Carrey in a simulated life that’s actually an enormous television studio manipulated by a god-like Ed Harris. It’s a clever film that turns everyday paranoia into a deeply unsettling existential nightmare — proceed with caution!
Where to watch The Truman Show : Pluto TV
George Clooney is a fixer at an important NYC law firm dealing with the fallout of a panicked colleague. It turns out his company is knowingly aiding an agrochemical giant that is actively poisoning the planet, but to say anything would affect the bottom line. Tilda Swinton won the Best Supporting Actress Oscar for her portrayal of the ruthless exec who only shows frailty and humanity in the mirror.
Where to watch Michael Clayton : Prime Video (to rent)
Using the Ted Kennedy Chappaquiddick scandal as a starting point, John Travolta stars as a sound mixer on low-budget films whose tape recorder may or may not capture evidence of a major government scandal. In addition to being a juicy conspiracy thriller, Blow Out is director Brian De Palma’s love letter to the handmade mechanics of filmmaking made all the more lovely in our less-tactile digital age.
Where to watch Blow Out : Prime Video
Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .
One of Alfred Hitchcock’s first major masterpieces, The 39 Steps features all the hallmarks of great, moody, paranoid filmmaking. A Canadian visitor to Britain stumbles into an international spy ring, and finds himself on the run in the Scottish Highlands. Along the way he ends up handcuffed to a damsel, leading to numerous scenes of comedy, plus a marvelous twist ending that is elegantly seeded earlier in the film.
Where to watch The 39 Steps : HBO Max
The Parallax View is one of the great paranoid thrillers of the Watergate era, in which it was just accepted that the CIA were out there assassinating political candidates and no one was telling the truth. Warren Beatty plays a reporter who is this close to uncovering the great violent scandal of our time. The true stars, however, are director Alan J. Pakula, cinematographer Gordon Willis, and production designer George Jenkins, who capture mid-’70s America as if visiting from another planet.
Where to watch The Parallax View : Pluto TV
Kevin Costner plays a Navy officer who begins an affair with a mysterious woman played by Sean Young, later revealed to be the mistress of the Secretary of Defense, played by Gene Hackman. When she ends up dead, he is assigned to investigate. As he does so, he discovers that the chief suspect is: himself. Uh-oh! Costner in a sailor suit did great things for this movie’s box office.
Robert Redford has a weird job at the beginning of this paranoid classic — he reads books all day. What he’s actually doing is scanning for hidden codes from foreign agents. And then one day, he finds something, but it’s not what the government wants him to see. Soon he’s racing for his life (and shacked up with Faye Dunaway), ultimately facing down multinational corporations, the CIA, Max von Sydow, and the corrupt press. Scary!
Where to watch Three Days of the Condor : YouTube
In life, you are either Rowdy Roddy Piper begging people to look through your magic sunglasses or Keith David refusing at all costs. This low-budget sci-fi exploitation film from John Carpenter is one of the more sly conspiracy thrillers out there. It points the finger at mindless consumerism and commercialism, and features so many iconic images that younger viewers may not even realize they come from a movie.
Where to watch They Live : Prime Video
John le Carré’s espionage masterpiece goes inside “The Circus,” the code name for British intelligence. Gary Oldman is Smiley, the close-to-the-vest veteran brought back to suss out a Soviet mole. Every British actor of the era — Benedict Cumberbatch, Tom Hardy, Colin Firth, Mark Strong, and more — makes a taciturn appearance in this secretive movie that all snaps together at the end.
Where to watch Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy : Fandango (to rent)
Robert Towne and Roman Polanski’s marvelous collaboration is a salute to Hollywood’s great noir films of the past as well as the darkness of that city’s foundation. Jack Nicholson gives one of his all-time great performances as a gruff private detective who foolishly falls in love with the woman he’s trying to rescue, played by Faye Dunaway. Director John Huston is perfectly cast as the monstrous villain behind a grotesque conspiracy based on documented facts.
Alfred Hitchcock went to the “wrong man wrapped up in a conspiracy” well many times, but never so perfectly as with North by Northwest . Cary Grant is an affable Madison Avenue ad exec who accidentally answers the call of fate and ends up racing from Long Island mansions to the top of Mount Rushmore, dodging bullets in a midwestern cornfield along the way. The movie is utterly preposterous, but its breathless, propulsive nature earns it its legendary status.
Where to watch North by Northwest : Tubi
This is the grand paranoid conspiracy thriller that turned out to be absolutely true and changed modern history. Robert Redford and Dustin Hoffman are the scrappy young journalists Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein, who tug at a story that doesn’t quite make sense until the entire presidency falls. Director Alan J. Pakula, cinematographer Gordon Willis, and screenwriter William Goldman took everything from The Parallax View and made it better, producing one of the greatest motion pictures ever made.
Where to watch All the President’s Men : YouTube
